name: Highlands 19

nadir.desc: The nadir view shows a single-story residence set well back from the road on a large desert scrub parcel densely vegetated with juniper trees across all sides|A paved driveway connects the property to what appears to be an intersection of two roads on the right side of the image, with the driveway curving through the juniper-covered lot to a circular or looped parking area in front of the structure|A blue and red sport court is visible immediately adjacent to the main structure, and a detached structure or garage is visible to the left of the main building|The rear of the property shows a landscaped green lawn area and what appears to be a patio or pergola structure.

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from the street side, with a paved road running along the lower edge of the image|Dense juniper trees cover the approach to the residence from the front, obscuring direct sightlines to the structure from the street|Only a very small portion of the residence is visible through the tree canopy near the center of the view.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the right side of the property from an oblique angle, with dense juniper trees dominating the entire field of view|The residence is largely hidden behind the tree canopy from this perspective, with only a faint roofline discernible near the center of the image|The terrain across the right side of the parcel is open desert scrub with no visible fencing, outbuildings, or secondary access routes on this side.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, with the main residence visible near the center of the image surrounded closely by juniper trees on all sides|The roofline of the single-story structure is low-pitched and tan or earth-toned, consistent with the nadir view|Tree coverage directly adjacent to the rear and sides of the structure is dense, and no rear access road or gate is visible from this perspective.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property with a paved road or driveway visible along the left edge of the image|Dense juniper trees cover the majority of the left side of the parcel, and the main structure is partially visible through the canopy near the center-right of the view|No fencing, secondary structures, or additional access points are identifiable on the left side of the property.

considerations: The property is set back a significant distance from the public road, accessed by a single paved driveway that curves through dense juniper vegetation before reaching the residence. Dense juniper tree coverage on all sides of the structure will limit visibility and sightlines from the road and from all approach angles, and trees grow in close proximity to the building itself. The circular driveway area near the front of the structure provides a staging area, but the narrow, curved access drive through heavy vegetation constrains large apparatus movement. Responders approaching from the rear or sides of the structure will encounter unimproved desert terrain with no visible secondary access routes.
clarifications: Is the driveway entrance from Macalpine Loop controlled by a gate, and if so, what is the gate width and access method? What is the surface width and weight-bearing capacity of the driveway for large emergency vehicles? Are there any secondary foot or vehicle access paths to the rear or sides of the structure? Is the detached structure to the left of the main residence a garage, and does it connect internally to the main house? Are there any propane tanks, fuel storage, or other utilities located on the property that are not visible from aerial imagery?
